summary: Solver-facing instruction and referenced contract docs read as a coherent engineering handoff: drift-off-contract framing, binding doc pointer, and four responsibility-grouped bullets. Jira/Slack handoff passes; reverse-outline risk is low; no material AI cadence, inflated claims, or solver-facing leakage.

evidence.observation: Two short paragraphs plus four bullets. Opens with product location and drifted behavior, points at /app/outbox/docs/delivery-contract.md, then groups env wiring, boot/UI/seed, core delivery invariants, and UI/acceptance. No benchmark preamble, verifier talk, or one-bullet-per-test inventory.

Ordinary API/ops contract organized by product surface (env, auth, tenants, endpoints, events, attempts, audit, CLI, UI). Technical density is appropriate for a binding contract, not a second prompt or repair map.
Brief operator notes on binaries, sync mode, and seeded catalog; selective and non-rubric.

Difficulty/solution/verification notes explain coupled invariants without a file-by-file oracle. Mild packaging lead-in ('Edition 3 large-system task') is reviewer-facing boilerplate, not material solver-facing synthetic cadence.

Instruction matches human patterns: selective end-state/work request, contract reference instead of schema dump, no essay transitions or reviewer-facing leakage. Mild feature lists in the opener and bullet 3 are within normal contract-alignment tickets, not compressed-rubric construction.

findings.why_it_matters: Submission README opens with Edition 3 packaging language; not solver-facing and not enough alone to fail handoff quality.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: rephrase the README lead-in as a plain product/system description without Edition 3 framing.
findings.regression_risk: None if left as-is; cosmetic only.

do_not_change: Do not thin instruction.md or move material work-request goals into delivery-contract.md merely for stylistic minimalism.
Do not rewrite delivery-contract.md into informal prose; keep it as a normal binding technical contract.
